name: Musée Fabre
aliases: Musée Fabre de Montpellier Méditerranée Métropole
overview: Fine arts museum on boulevard Bonne Nouvelle in Montpellier, with a decorative arts department in the Hôtel de Cabrières-Sabatier d'Espeyran; a large renovation was completed in 2007 (museum website).

Founded in 1825 by the painter François-Xavier Fabre (1766-1837), after a first museum of the Revolution years and the Société des Beaux-Arts de Montpellier of 1779; open to the public since 1828 (museum website; France 3 Occitanie, January 2025).

What is there: Flemish and Dutch painting from Fabre's gifts and the bequest of the stockbroker Antoine Valedau (1777-1836); 19th century French painting given mostly by Alfred Bruyas (1821-1877), including Courbet's La Rencontre and Les Baigneuses; works by the Montpellier painters Alexandre Cabanel and Frédéric Bazille; a group of works by Pierre Soulages; and 18th century Montpellier silver (museum website). The pages read did not give a total number of works.
funding_verdict: Musée Fabre: public, Montpellier's local authorities; a company foundation funds acquisitions

name: Musée d'arts de Nantes
overview: Fine arts museum at 10 rue Georges Clemenceau in central Nantes, formerly the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Nantes; a musée de France since 5 January 2002 (Museofile record; Le Voyage à Nantes).

Founding: the Museofile record dates the consular order creating the museum to 1800; Apollo dates the Chaptal decree to 1801, and Le Voyage à Nantes also gives 1801. The City bought the Cacault collection in 1810, the works went on show in the Halle aux toiles in 1830, and a new palace by the Nantes-born architect Clément-Marie Josso opened in 1900 (Museofile record; Apollo, 26 June 2017).
The seventeenth-century Chapelle de l'Oratoire was restored and given to the museum in 1988 (Apollo).
funding_verdict: Musée d'arts de Nantes: public: Nantes Métropole, with 2017 renovation money from the EU, the State, the Region, the Département and the City

name: Cité de l'architecture et du patrimoine
aliases: Cité de l'architecture et du patrimoine (Palais de Chaillot)
overview: The Cité de l'architecture et du patrimoine is at the Palais de Chaillot, Place du Trocadéro, and is part of the Ministry of Culture (institution's website).
The pages read do not give a founding date.

What is there: the Cast Gallery of the Musée des Monuments français, a Modern and Contemporary Architecture Gallery and a Murals and Stained Glass Gallery (institution's website). The 2021 report counts 4,000 architectural casts and 350 reproductions of murals.
funding_verdict: Cité de l'architecture et du patrimoine: mainly public, State grant with about one sixth own income

name: Musée d'Art Moderne de Paris
aliases: Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris
overview: The City of Paris's museum of 20th and 21st century art at 11, avenue du Président-Wilson, in a building made for the Exposition internationale des arts et des techniques of 1937 (Paris Musées annual report 2025).

It was inaugurated in 1961, an opening made possible by the bequest of 533 works from the dealer Maurice Girardin, reopened after renovation in 2019 and has been run by Paris Musées since 2013 (Paris Musées annual report 2025; The Art Newspaper, 13 June 2025).

The collection holds close to 16 000 works covering fauvism, cubism, the École de Paris, abstraction, nouveau réalisme, figuration narrative and conceptual art, with two works made for the site, Raoul Dufy's La Fée Électricité and Matisse's La Danse; it has received over 800 works since 2007, including gifts from the estates of Josef Albers and Zao Wou-Ki and Michael Werner's gift of 127 works in 2012 (Paris Musées annual report 2025; The Art Newspaper, 13 June 2025).
funding_verdict: Musée d'Art Moderne de Paris: mainly public, paid by the City of Paris through Paris Musées, with corporate exhibition patrons and dealer gifts

name: Musée de l'Orangerie
aliases: Établissement public du musée d'Orsay et du musée de l'Orangerie
overview: National museum in the former orangery of the Tuileries garden, on the Seine side of place de la Concorde, Paris (museum website).

Claude Monet offered the Nymphéas to France the day after the armistice of 11 November 1918; they were installed to his plans in 1927, a few months after his death. Since 2010 the museum has formed one public establishment with the Musée d'Orsay (museum website; EPMO website).

What is there: Monet's Nymphéas cycle, and the Jean Walter and Paul Guillaume collection of 148 works from the 1860s to the 1930s: 25 Renoir, 15 Cézanne, 12 Picasso, 10 Matisse, 5 Modigliani, 9 Douanier Rousseau, 30 Derain, 22 Soutine, 10 Utrillo, 6 Marie Laurencin. The dealer Paul Guillaume formed it between 1914 and his death in 1934; his widow Domenica, remarried to the architect and industrialist Jean Walter, 'transformed and reduced' it and made new purchases; the state acquired it in 1959 and 1963 subject to her life interest, and she kept the pictures until 1977 (museum website).
funding_verdict: Musée de l'Orangerie: public establishment shared with Orsay, about three fifths self-earned, the rest a state grant

name: Théâtre de la Ville
aliases: Théâtre de la Ville - Sarah Bernhardt
overview: The Théâtre de la Ville is a Paris theatre association with venues on the Place du Châtelet (Sarah Bernhardt) and Les Abbesses, and it works with partner theatres including Chaillot and the Théâtre de la Cité internationale (theatre website; 2026-27 brochure).
The theatre on the Place du Châtelet burned in the Paris Commune in 1871 and was rebuilt; in 1968 its interior was demolished and replaced, leaving the four Second Empire walls (theatre website).

What is there: the house presents theatre, dance and music; the director is Emmanuel Demarcy-Mota, who has worked with a resident troupe for more than twenty years (theatre website). Programme includes festivals and a Places festival in the city's squares (2026-27 brochure).
funding_verdict: Théâtre de la Ville: public subsidy from the City of Paris plus named foundation and corporate partners; amounts not given

name: Akademie der Künste
overview: The Akademie der Künste is a society of artists and a federal cultural institution in Berlin, with houses at Pariser Platz 4 and at Hanseatenweg 10 in the Tiergarten (Akademie website).

Elector Friedrich III of Brandenburg founded it in 1696; an East Berlin academy was founded in 1950 and a West Berlin one first met in 1956, the two were joined under a Berlin and Brandenburg state treaty in force from 1 October 1993, and the federal government took the Akademie over in 2005, the year the new building at Pariser Platz by Günter Behnisch with Werner Durth opened (Akademie website, history page).

What is there: no art museum collection in the usual sense, the members run the programme in six sections (visual arts, architecture, music, literature, performing arts, film and media art); the house at Hanseatenweg was given by the German-American Henry H. Reichhold and designed by Werner Düttmann (Akademie website).
funding_verdict: Akademie der Künste: public, carried by the federal government
wider_context: Bundestag antisemitism resolution: on 29 August 2024 the Akademie, with other cultural associations, said the publicly discussed draft of 'Nie wieder ist jetzt: Jüdisches Leben in Deutschland schützen, bewahren und stärken' 'risks doing more harm than providing protection', objected to legal clauses in funding practice and asked the Bundestag to suspend adoption (Akademie website, 29 August 2024).

The Bundestag adopted the non-binding resolution on 7 November 2024 with the votes of CDU/CSU, SPD, Greens, FDP and AfD; it commits to the IHRA definition and asks for stricter antisemitism conditions on state funding, and Josef Schuster of the Zentralrat der Juden said 'Die Grundlagen für einen wirksamen Schutz jüdischen Lebens sind nun definiert' (Jüdische Allgemeine, 7 November 2024).

name: Altes Museum
overview: Museum of classical antiquity on the Lustgarten, Museum Island, Berlin; it houses the Antikensammlung of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and part of the Münzkabinett (museum website).

Karl Friedrich Schinkel's building went up from 1823 to 1830, with 18 fluted Ionic columns and a rotunda modelled on the Roman Pantheon; the foundation stone was laid on 9 July 1825 and the museum opened on 3 August 1830 as the first public museum in Berlin and Prussia (museum website).
The inscription over the columns says Friedrich Wilhelm III founded the museum in 1828 for the study of antiquities and the liberal arts (museum website).
funding_verdict: Altes Museum: public: the German federal government and the states through the Stiftung Preußischer Kulturbesitz
wider_context: During the Second World War the Berlin museums moved objects to bunkers; at the end of the war the Red Army seized all of the Antikensammlung's art objects then in Berlin and took them to Moscow or Leningrad (museum website, Antikensammlung page).
In 1958 the Soviet Union returned one and a half million works of art to the GDR, including the Pergamon Altar frieze panels (museum website).
The Antikensammlung, which lost these objects, is the collection shown in the Altes Museum today.

name: Berliner Festspiele
aliases: Kulturveranstaltungen des Bundes in Berlin GmbH
overview: Berliner Festspiele organises festivals, exhibitions, concerts, dance and theatre through the year, in the Haus der Berliner Festspiele at Schaperstraße 24 and the Gropius Bau at Niederkirchnerstraße 7 (Berliner Festspiele website).

The Berliner Festwochen were started in 1951, in the same year as the Berlin film festival; under the capital culture treaty the federal government became sole shareholder of Berliner Festspiele GmbH in 2001, and KBB was formed with effect from 1 January 2002 by merger with Haus der Kulturen der Welt GmbH (KBB website, history page). The institution marks its 75th anniversary in 2026 (Berliner Festspiele website).

What is there: the Haus der Berliner Festspiele, built by Fritz Bornemann and opened on 1 May 1963 as the Theater der Freien Volksbühne, a 1,000-seat theatre the Festspiele moved into in December 2000 and reopened on 21 April 2001; the programme is Theatertreffen, Musikfest Berlin, MaerzMusik, Jazzfest Berlin, the Performing Arts Season, Reflexe und Reflexionen and the youth contests of Treffen junge Szene (Berliner Festspiele website).
funding_verdict: Berliner Festspiele: public, a division of a federal company

name: Deutsche Oper Berlin
overview: Opera house on Bismarckstraße in Charlottenburg, Berlin, and the city's largest opera house, with 1,859 seats (berlin.de; German Music Information Centre, miz.org).
The then independent City of Charlottenburg opened the first house, the Deutsches Opernhaus, in 1912; a bombing raid on 23 November 1943 destroyed most of it (berlin.de).
Building: the company reopened under its present name on 24 September 1961 in Fritz Bornemann's new house on the same street (berlin.de).
funding_verdict: Deutsche Oper Berlin: public: the State of Berlin through the Stiftung Oper in Berlin

press_items.title: Peter Uehling, "Die Spielzeit an der Deutschen Oper: Heißer Scheiß im Glanz des Gestrigen" (14 April 2026)

name: Flutgraben
overview: Self-organised, non-profit artists' studio house at Am Flutgraben 3, 12435 Berlin, on the Treptow side of the Flutgraben canal that separates Kreuzberg and Treptow (visitBerlin, Flutgraben).

The association was founded in 1997 as "Kunstfabrik am Flutgraben" and runs the house as Flutgraben e.V. (Flutgraben). Since 2004 it has also managed the former watch tower at Schlesischer Busch, which the initiative The Watch uses for exhibitions, lectures, screenings and residencies (Flutgraben).

The building is a former workshop of VEB OLW in brick, on the border with West Berlin. The Berlin State Monuments Office calls it the only East Berlin border house that survived the expansion of the border fortifications. Roof catwalks were built in 1988, and the 1990s facade renovation preserved traces of the border (Landesdenkmalamt).
funding_verdict: Flutgraben: self-funded: studio rents and room hire

press_items.title: Ingeborg Ruthe, "Herrscht etwa Darwinismus im Atelierhaus Flutgraben e.V.?" (8 December 2023)

name: Gemäldegalerie
overview: The Gemäldegalerie is the Old Master painting gallery of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, at the Kulturforum since 1998 in a building by Hilmer & Sattler, who won the competition announced in 1986 (museum website).

It was established as a public institution in 1830 in Schinkel's Königliches Museum am Lustgarten, today the Altes Museum; its basis was the art holdings of the Great Elector and Frederick the Great (museum website).

What is there: European painting from the 13th to the 18th century, about 1,200 works on show in 72 halls and cabinets along a route of nearly two kilometres; strengths in German and Italian painting of the 13th to 16th centuries and Netherlandish painting of the 15th to 17th centuries; 20 works by Rembrandt; named works include Caravaggio's 'Amor als Sieger' (1602), Cranach's 'Der Jungbrunnen' (1546), Giotto's 'Die Grablegung Mariae', Titian's 'Venus mit dem Orgelspieler' and Vermeer's 'Junge Dame mit Perlenhalsband' (museum website).
funding_verdict: Gemäldegalerie: public, through the Stiftung Preußischer Kulturbesitz (federal government and the Länder)

name: Gropius Bau
overview: Exhibition house for large temporary exhibitions at 7 Niederkirchnerstrasse in Berlin-Kreuzberg (Wikipedia).
Built from 1877 to 1881 in neo-Renaissance style by the architects Martin Gropius and Heino Schmieden, and named for Gropius. It first housed the Museum of Applied Arts (Wikipedia).

Heavily damaged in 1945. The German Wikipedia says the Berlin Wall stood directly in front of the main entrance from 1961 to 1989. Declared a historic monument in 1966, rebuilt from 1978, and reopened in 1981 with a Schinkel exhibition (Wikipedia, German Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Gropius Bau: mainly public: German federal government through the Berliner Festspiele, with money raised per exhibition

name: Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen
overview: The state museum of North Rhine-Westphalia for art from the early twentieth century onward, in Düsseldorf, in two buildings: K20 at Grabbeplatz 5, by Dissing+Weitling, and K21 in the Ständehaus, the former state parliament building, converted by Kiessler Architekten (museum website; collection website).

Founded in 1961 as Stiftung Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen after the state bought 88 works by Paul Klee in 1960 from the collection of the American industrialist G. David Thompson; Werner Schmalenbach was founding director; K20 opened in 1986 and K21 in 2002 (collection website).

The collection: works by Beckmann, Braque, Ernst, Kirchner, Matisse, Mondrian, Picasso, Rauschenberg and Warhol, Jackson Pollock's Number 32 (1950, acquired 1964) and Joseph Beuys's Palazzo Regale (1985, acquired 1993); the Ackermans Collection of more than 150 works came in 2004 and the Fischer Collection of Minimal and Conceptual art between 2013 and 2015. The page gives no total and no purchase prices (collection website).
funding_verdict: Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen: mainly public, a state museum, plus corporate partners and foundations
wider_context: The collection website notes that Nazi authorities dismissed Paul Klee from the Düsseldorf Academy in 1933 and that his works were among those defamed as 'degenerate'; the state's 1960 purchase of 88 Klee works is the founding act of the collection (collection website).

name: Oper Frankfurt
overview: Oper Frankfurt is the opera of the Städtische Bühnen Frankfurt am Main GmbH at Willy-Brandt-Platz, in a building opened in 1902 with later phases in 1951 and 1963, gross floor area 49,730 m2 (miz.org).
Its Generalmusikdirektor is Thomas Guggeis; the Frankfurter Opern- und Museumsorchester, Chor, Kinderchor, Opernstudio and Paul-Hindemith-Orchesterakademie are listed on its site (opera website).

What is there: the repertoire on the site includes Ottone, Hänsel und Gretel, Le roi Arthus, Un ballo in maschera, Così fan tutte and Salome, with Andrea Breth and Barrie Kosky among the directors named (opera website).
funding_verdict: Oper Frankfurt: public, through the Städtische Bühnen GmbH; amounts not stated on the pages read

name: Sprengel Museum Hannover
overview: The Sprengel Museum Hannover is a museum of international art of the 20th and 21st centuries with 8,000 square metres of exhibition space (museum website).

It began with the gift of Margrit and Bernhard Sprengel, who in 1969 gave their collection of modern art to the City of Hanover and a sum towards the building; the first section opened in June 1979, and until 1984 it was called 'Kunstmuseum Hannover mit Sammlung Sprengel' (museum website).

What is there: 49,200 inventoried works and documents, of which 9,022 are gifts and 14,498 permanent loans: 2,037 paintings, 1,526 sculptures, 25,999 drawings and prints and 13,374 photographs and media works; the holdings join the Sprengel collection with the 20th century art of the city and the state, with focuses on Paul Klee, Emil Nolde, Max Beckmann, the 'Brücke' and the 'Blauer Reiter' (museum website).
funding_verdict: Sprengel Museum Hannover: public, shared by the City of Hanover and the State of Lower Saxony, with foundation support

name: Staatliche Kunsthalle Karlsruhe
overview: The Staatliche Kunsthalle Karlsruhe is one of the oldest museum buildings in Germany and a protected monument; the main building is closed for renovation and exhibitions take place at the ZKM, the Orangerie and the Junge Kunsthalle (museum website; Land press release).
The museum calls itself one of Germany's largest and most historical art museums and 'an institution of the State of Baden-Württemberg' (museum website). The pages read did not give a founding year.
What is there: collection highlights are shown online; the pages read gave no object count (museum website).
funding_verdict: Staatliche Kunsthalle Karlsruhe: public, state of Baden-Württemberg

name: Kölner Philharmonie
overview: The Kölner Philharmonie is a concert hall opened in 1986, the main hall lying underground beneath the Heinrich-Böll-Platz (Philharmonie website).
The concert programming is run by KölnMusik Betriebs- und Servicegesellschaft mbH; Ewa Bogusz-Moore is Artistic Director and Managing Director (KölnMusik GmbH page).
What is there: symphonies, jazz, folk and pop, premieres and children's concerts; the WDR Sinfonieorchester and the Gürzenich-Orchester Köln are the two house orchestras (Philharmonie website).
funding_verdict: Kölner Philharmonie: public, through KölnMusik GmbH with City of Cologne and WDR on its supervisory board; sums not stated on the pages read

name: Museum der bildenden Künste Leipzig
overview: The Museum der bildenden Künste Leipzig (MdbK) is the city's art museum, in a building on Katharinenstraße opened on 4 December 2004, with courtyards and parts of the permanent display open free of charge (museum website).

The Leipziger Kunstverein was founded in 1837 to build a collection; the 'Städtisches Museum' was set up in 1848 and moved in 1858 to a new building on Augustusplatz paid for by the bequest of Adolf Heinrich Schletter, who left the city assets and his collection in 1853 (museum website).

What is there: over 4,600 paintings, 1,800 sculptures, medals and plaques, over 5,000 photographs and over 70,000 works on paper, from Old Masters such as Frans Hals and Lucas Cranach the Younger to Caspar David Friedrich, Max Beckmann and Max Klinger, with Leipzig art and art of the GDR as a focus; nearly 400 paintings are Dutch 17th century works (museum website).
funding_verdict: Museum der bildenden Künste Leipzig: city museum, with foundation-owned holdings
wider_context: In June 2019 a panel on the Leipziger Jahresausstellung fell through when the painter Axel Krause, criticised for his closeness to the AfD, cancelled on 10 June; he had made the psychologist Hans-Joachim Maaz's participation a condition and blamed the then MdbK director Alfred Weidinger (Leipziger Zeitung, 10 June 2019).

name: BMW Museum
overview: The BMW Museum is the company museum of BMW in Munich, with houses on company history, design, technology and motorsport and an Art Car Gallery (BMW Welt page).
It opened on 18 May 1973, closed in 2004 for renovation and reopened in June 2008 (BMW newsroom).

What is there: 5,000 square metres of exhibition in seven themed houses with rotating special exhibitions; a temporary show, Belle Macchine, is listed until the end of 2026. The pages read gave no object or vehicle count (BMW newsroom, BMW Welt page).
funding_verdict: BMW Museum: paid by the company; no budget published on the pages read.
